purpose: Evaluate a small, fixed pilot of Veda research reports against primary empirical studies and independent human review. This is not a representative sample and cannot support a population-wide accuracy claim.

selection_method.selection_basis: Cover distinct research tasks and intentionally include positive, null or heterogeneous, and negative evidence. Include both task-level and organizational outcomes; prefer primary empirical work with identifiable populations, designs, outcomes, and accessible source text.
anti_selection_rules: Do not replace a selected case after observing Veda output or scores.
If a selected case or candidate source proves unusable, record the reason and retain it as missing or protocol deviation; any replacement must be added as a dated amendment before its run.
Do not treat the selected cases as random, representative, or exhaustive.
Do not turn these source mappings into gold answers; reviewers must independently inspect the actual source and report.

cases.reason_selected: A controlled coding study offers a positive/task-level contrast against the selected negative experienced-developer study; prevent coding speed from being equated with end-to-end delivery.

candidate_primary_sources.citation: Peng et al. (2023), The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
candidate_primary_sources.access_status: arXiv v1 metadata, HTML/PDF access, and version checked; full-text methodological review pending; downstream reuse rights not established

cases.stratum: measurement sensitivity and negative developer result
cases.reason_selected: The primary RCT compares experienced developers' expectations with observed task completion time, testing whether perceived productivity and measured completion diverge.

candidate_primary_sources.citation: Becker et al. (2025), Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
candidate_primary_sources.source_role: primary randomized controlled trial on experienced open-source developers
candidate_primary_sources.access_status: arXiv v2 metadata, HTML/PDF access, and CC BY 4.0 terms checked; full-text methodological review and independent gold-source validation pending

cases.reason_selected: Professional writing tasks provide evidence for one bounded domain and test whether a system improperly generalizes the estimate to sectors or occupations not studied.

candidate_primary_sources.citation: Noy and Zhang (2023), Experimental Evidence on the Productivity Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidate_primary_sources.access_status: Science final-article DOI path returned HTTP 403 in this audit; accessible MIT working-paper PDF is a distinct 2023 non-peer-reviewed version (n=444); final-version full text, equivalence, and reuse rights unresolved

cases.stratum: consulting evidence and conditional task performance
cases.reason_selected: A randomized experiment among knowledge workers supports checking task-specific benefits, quality, and failures without extrapolating bounded consultant tasks to enterprise ROI.

candidate_primary_sources.citation: Dell’Acqua et al. (2026), Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier: Field Experimental Evidence of the Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Knowledge Worker Productivity and Quality
candidate_primary_sources.source_role: primary preregistered randomized field experiment of knowledge workers
candidate_primary_sources.access_status: 2026 publisher version and publisher HTML/PDF access checked; CC BY 4.0 stated; independent gold-source validation and embedded-third-party screening pending

cases.reason_selected: A workplace deployment with agent-level operational outcomes tests handling throughput and broader customer/worker measures beyond bounded laboratory tasks.

candidate_primary_sources.citation: Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond (2025), Generative AI at Work
candidate_primary_sources.source_role: primary workplace study of a staggered assistant rollout among customer-support agents
candidate_primary_sources.access_status: publisher full text reported open; verify exact paper version and inspect limitations

cases.reason_selected: The same prespecified support study has experience-stratified outcomes, allowing a second case to test whether Veda distinguishes average from subgroup results without treating correlated cases as independent studies.

candidate_primary_sources.citation: Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond (2025), Generative AI at Work
candidate_primary_sources.source_role: same primary workplace study as SUP01; dependent case/source reuse is explicitly recorded
candidate_primary_sources.access_status: publisher article/version and full-text access checked; CC BY-NC 4.0 stated; use-specific noncommercial classification pending; same study maps SUP01 and SUP02

cases.stratum: small-firm financial return and heterogeneous null result
cases.reason_selected: A field experiment measures business performance and exposes a null average effect with baseline-performance heterogeneity; test whether Veda preserves the denominator, uncertainty, and subgroup qualification.

candidate_primary_sources.citation: Otis et al. (2026), The Uneven Impact of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Entrepreneurial Performance: Evidence from a Field Experiment in Kenya
candidate_primary_sources.source_role: primary randomized field experiment with small-business entrepreneurs
candidate_primary_sources.access_status: 2026 publisher Articles-in-Advance version and publisher HTML/PDF access checked; CC BY 4.0 stated; earlier manuscript not version-matched; independent gold-source validation pending

include: Primary empirical studies that report their own data, sample, design, intervention/exposure, comparator, outcome, and limits relevant to the selected case.
Versioned author manuscripts or publisher versions only when the precise version and access class are recorded.
A source can be used as a counterexample or scope boundary even when it does not directly answer the selected question, but that role must be explicit.
exclude_from_primary_evidence_set: Press releases, news, consultancy estimates, narrative summaries, and secondary reviews (may be logged as discovery leads but not as primary evidence).
Abstract-only records when a passage-level claim or method requires unavailable full text; retain them with abstract-only access status, not as full-text reviewed.
Sources whose identity, version, population, comparator, or outcome cannot be verified.
Any material whose retrieval/reuse permission is unknown when the proposed use would require storing or reproducing full text. Metadata-only use may remain separately labeled.
per_source_required_review: access class, license/retrieval rights, and passages actually inspected

freeze_before_run: application source revision or source-tree SHA-256 manifest when Git revision is unavailable
provider, model identifier, provider-reported model version, prompt/schema versions, depth profile, source limits, and execution date
candidate-source set version and access status
query and provider-call ledger, including failed/empty queries
all immutable report, source, passage, claim, comparison, citation-audit, and usage artifacts
run_capture.secrets: Never store API keys, bearer tokens, personal reviewer identities, or raw authorization headers in the run manifest.
run_capture.cost: Capture provider-reported amounts and token usage separately from local estimates. Unknown is not zero. A run without a verifiable provider cost observation remains cost-missing.

review.reviewers: Use two independent reviewers with relevant subject/method expertise. Store only an assigned pseudonym, role, expertise area, date, and conflict declaration in records; keep identity mapping outside the repository.
review.blindness: Reviewers score independently before seeing each other's scores or any consensus summary. They inspect the report and underlying source/passage, not only citation presence or model labels.
review.adjudication: Log disagreements by dimension and finding; a third qualified reviewer resolves material disagreements. Preserve both original records. Do not overwrite independent scores with consensus.
review.synthetic_fixture: evaluation/annotations/schema-only-example.json is solely a schema fixture and is never included in the human-reviewed denominator.

metrics.numerator: reviewer-confirmed eligible primary studies in the predeclared case source set retrieved and correctly identified in the Veda run's top k
metrics.denominator: eligible primary studies in that case's final reviewer-validated source set
metrics.rule: A source is not eligible solely because it appears in this candidate file; reviewers may exclude it with reason before examining run scores. Report missing/unavailable studies and denominators explicitly.

metrics.numerator: sampled material report claims independently judged substantively supported by the cited saved source passage at the stated scope
metrics.denominator: all sampled material claims, including unsupported, wrong-source, missing-passage, and not-assessable items, each disposition reported separately

metrics.numerator: material factual claims with a resolvable, relevant source and passage
metrics.denominator: all material factual claims independently identified in the report

metrics.numerator: reviewed claims that preserve study population, setting, design, comparator, outcomes, denominator, and horizon as applicable
metrics.denominator: all reviewed claims where those dimensions are assessable; publish dimension-specific missing/N/A counts

metrics.numerator: reviewer-identified eligible counterevidence sources or material findings surfaced with accurate scope
metrics.denominator: all reviewer-identified eligible counterevidence sources or material findings in the frozen set
reviewer-by-case-run score records per dimension; N/A is excluded from the numeric mean and reported separately

metrics.numerator: provider-reported cost for that immutable run; separately report any estimate
metrics.denominator: completed runs with an observed provider-reported cost; missing-cost runs are counted separately and never assigned zero

aggregation_and_interpretation.same_source_reuse: SUP01 and SUP02 share a study and are not independent evidence replications; show per-case results but do not count them as two independent studies.
aggregation_and_interpretation.publish: Include case selection, source inclusion/exclusion, run failures, missing data, all dimension denominators, reviewer disagreements, adjudications, access class, provider/model versions, and cost coverage.
prohibited_claims: Do not call synthetic fixtures a research-quality benchmark.
Do not call this seven-case purposive pilot an accuracy rate or general performance estimate.
Do not claim expert review, source recall, support, omission, or cost scores before actual runs and independent reviewers exist.
Do not equate schema validation or an automated semantic audit with human verification.

open_requirements: Case-specific content review and independent gold-source validation remain pending; Noy–Zhang final Science full text/version/terms are unresolved, and Brynjolfsson passage use requires a Veda-specific noncommercial-use determination or permission. See the candidate metadata/version/access screen note.
Run one complete Veda job for every selected case with a newly rotated, securely configured free-model credential and zero-cost enforcement; do not reuse the key exposed in chat.
Obtain two independent qualified reviewers per completed case-run, then preserve disagreements and adjudication records.
Populate results with observed run artifacts and explicit numerators and denominators.
